findings.reason: the followup is the only driving instruction, so a section missing from it is work nobody queues until a coordinator notices by hand.
findings.text: the open followup lists "§2–§16 and §19–§25" as the batch to queue and names §28 nowhere, while plan-section-declarations declares s28 implementable; a coordinator obeying the followup leaves the new section undispatched, and the gap already open for §26 and §27 now covers a third section

findings.reason: the case needs either disjoint declared write paths stated for the two requests or a declared wait on §23, without which the gate fails on the overlap rule and the control proves nothing about answered findings.
findings.text: §28's first case requires that two requests queued on one section are both admitted at the next pass, but the base holds a later queued request behind an earlier one whose declared write paths overlap by containment in the same repository (reckon/crew/admission/holds.py:_queued_requests_overlap), which two requests derived from one section's sentence share; with §23 open and no dependency declared, the second request stays held at head for a reason this section does not change, and at base the same overlap hold makes the negative control read as passing evidence of the review hold it never exercised

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §28 cites only its evidence fragment path under the repository's evidence directory, consistent with the sibling sections; the declarations and section id s28 resolve in the snapshot.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §28's first case at plan.html:329 asserts "both requests are admitted", an arm admission already fails on the base's queued-request overlap rule (§23's subject), so the case cannot go green on this section's change alone and the negative control cannot show the review hold fires.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §28's failing run is logged to docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/s28.html beside the other sections' fragments, not a node-local or session path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §28's endpoint language is mechanism-first ("a finding is answered as acted on", "stay covered by that review") and carries no plan label, stage name or ticket id.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the Why matches the cited behaviour on all three checks: admission does hold a request whose section moved and release it only when the gate passes again (reckon/crew/admission/reviews.py:_release_plan_review_holds, reckon/crew/routing.py:require_plan_reviewed), and answering a finding persists a finding disposition without recording the acceptance that coverage reads (reckon/crew/review_dispositions.py, plan_review._compute_coverage's acceptance clause), so the stated cause is accurate and the section names no code path, step sequence or function.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §28 carries one deliverable: an answered finding keeps its edited sections covered, with the later-unanswered-edit clause as the boundary of that same coverage rule.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the single open followup at plan.html:335 still dispatches only "§2–§16 and §19–§25", so the newly added §28 (declared implementable at plan.html:23) is in no dispatch list, the same gap already open for §26 and §27.
